Final Fantasy. A multimedia role-playing game franchise that debuted from Squaresoft in 1987, it's known for elaborate fantasy worlds, emotionally driven narratives, and turn-based combat systems that evolved into real-time mechanics. The series pioneered JRPG storytelling and has evolved across sixteen main entries, countless spin-offs, films, and remakes, exerting enormous influence on the entire genre. The franchise launched on the Nintendo Entertainment System in 1987, but Final Fantasy III in 1990 and Final Fantasy VI in 1994, both on SNES, introduced cinematic storytelling with ensemble casts and villain-driven narratives.

The cultural turning point came with Final Fantasy VII in 1997 for PlayStation. Cloud Strife, an ex-soldier protagonist, leads a ragtag resistance against the megacorporation Shinra and the god-like Sephiroth across a globe-spanning quest with catastrophic stakes. It became an absolute cultural touchstone. The franchise features a job system prominent in entries one, three, five, and ten, where players assign class-based roles like Knight, Mage, and Thief, shaping character abilities and team composition. Interestingly, the "Final Fantasy" title has nothing to do with numbering. Squaresoft named the first game believing it would be their last, so when it succeeded, each new entry got a new number but no direct plot connection to any other.

Final Fantasy X in 2001 introduced fully voice-acted characters, real-time combat segments called Active Time Battle, and the Sphere Grid character progression system. Final Fantasy XIV started in 2010 and was relaunched as A Realm Reborn in 2013 as a massively multiplayer online RPG that became a cultural phenomenon with an acclaimed narrative spanning expansions like Shadowbringers and Endwalker. The Final Fantasy VII Remake in 2020 is a full reimagining of the original, splitting the story across multiple installments and recontextualizing major plot points. Cloud Strife remains the main protagonist of FFVII and the face of the modern franchise, while Sephiroth stands as one of gaming's most iconic villains. Square Enix, formed when Squaresoft merged with Enix in 2003, continues to develop the series, having revolutionized storytelling depth in RPGs and popularizing turn-based combat as a foundational JRPG mechanic.
